successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy model file exposes a LeavePolicy interface and a CreateLeavePolicyDto, both importable from the leave module barrel (src/modules/leave/index.ts); the model imports LeaveType from the Phase 3 leave-type model to establish the cross-entity dependency.
repository.create persists a new leave policy row via the shared pg pool and returns the persisted record; when requiresManagerApproval or isActive are omitted from the DTO they default to true.

repository.findByLeaveTypeId returns all non-deleted policies for the given leave type id as an array (empty array when none exist), and repository.findById returns a single policy or null when not found.
repository.findAll returns all non-deleted leave policies as an array (empty array when the table has no active rows).

repository.update applies only the fields present in the partial DTO and returns the updated record; it returns null when the target does not exist, and returns the existing record unchanged when no fields are provided.
repository.softDelete marks the target row as deleted and returns true when a row was affected, false when the target does not exist or is already deleted.
The leave module barrel (src/modules/leave/index.ts) re-exports LeavePolicy, CreateLeavePolicyDto, ILeavePolicyRepository, and LeavePolicyRepository alongside the existing Phase 3 LeaveType exports.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave/leave-policy.repository.test.ts mock the shared pg pool and cover all six repository methods (findByLeaveTypeId, findById, findAll, create, update, softDelete) including not-found, empty-result, default-boolean, and empty-update edge cases.
The phase compiles under strict TypeScript (tsc --noEmit) with no implicit any and no type errors, and all Jest unit tests pass.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); the repository must use the shared pg pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts and never instantiate its own connection.
No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS no-any rule, severity high); strict TypeScript with strict null checks must pass.
The repository must be the only component that issues SQL against the leave_policies table; no inline SQL in services or controllers (GP-001).
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, API keys, or tokens (HARNESS no-hardcoded-secrets, severity critical).
No unhandled promise rejections — all async repository methods must propagate errors via returned/rejected promises without swallowing (GP-006).

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the leave-policy model may import LeaveType from the leave-type model within the same module, but external consumers must go through the barrel.
outOfScope: LeaveBalance model and repository (Phase 5) — not created or referenced in this phase.
LeaveRequest model and repository (Phase 6) — not created or referenced in this phase.
AuditLog model/repository and audit recording (Phase 7) — the repository does not write audit records; audit is a cross-cutting concern handled in later service phases.
Leave service, controller, and Fastify routes (Phases 8–9) — no service layer, HTTP endpoints, Zod validation, or RBAC enforcement in this phase.
Database migrations / DDL for the leave_policies table — this phase assumes the table schema exists; no migration files are produced.

Foreign-key validation of leaveTypeId against the leave_types table at the repository layer — the repository persists whatever DTO it receives; referential integrity enforcement belongs to the service layer in a later phase.

ambiguities.description: The reconciled architecture defines accrualRate, maxAccumulation, and minimumNoticeDays as `number | null`, but the PLAN.md Phase 4 task description and the current implementation use non-nullable `number`. Which nullability contract is authoritative for this phase?
options: Non-nullable number (matches PLAN.md task description and current code)

ambiguities.description: The model imports LeaveType from the leave-type model (as the task requires) but the LeavePolicy interface references leaveTypeId as a plain string rather than a typed LeaveType reference. The import is currently unused. Should the import be retained to satisfy the stated cross-entity dependency, or should leaveTypeId be typed against LeaveType['id']?
options: Retain the LeaveType import as-is to satisfy the stated dependency (leaveTypeId stays string)
Type leaveTypeId as LeaveType['id'] so the import is used
Remove the unused import to avoid dead code

ambiguities.description: The leave_policies table schema in the architecture lists no deleted_at column, yet the repository filters on `deleted_at IS NULL` for soft-delete (consistent with the leave_types and employees pattern). Should the soft-delete column be assumed present even though the conceptual schema omits it?
options: Assume deleted_at exists (consistent with leave_types/employees soft-delete pattern)
Omit deleted_at filtering to match the conceptual schema literally

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeavePolicy is logically deleted, never physically removed — softDelete sets a deleted timestamp and all read methods (findById, findAll, findByLeaveTypeId) exclude rows marked deleted; a deleted policy is never returned by read operations.

A LeavePolicy is associated with exactly one LeaveType via its leaveTypeId; the repository does not enforce referential integrity itself, but the association is a required, non-optional attribute on every persisted policy.

requiresManagerApproval and isActive are always defined on a persisted LeavePolicy — when omitted from the creation DTO they default to true, so no persisted policy has an undefined/null value for these flags.
A CreateLeavePolicyDto is a partial-input shape for creation: the numeric and identifying fields are required, while requiresManagerApproval and isActive are optional and default to true when absent.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns LeavePolicy[] (empty array when none); propagates pool errors as rejected promises.
Returns LeavePolicy | null (null when not found or deleted); propagates pool errors as rejected promises.
Returns LeavePolicy[] (empty array when none); propagates pool errors as rejected promises.
Returns the persisted LeavePolicy; defaults requiresManagerApproval and isActive to true when omitted; propagates pool/constraint errors as rejected promises.
Returns LeavePolicy | null (null when target missing/deleted); when no fields provided returns the existing record via findById without issuing an UPDATE; propagates pool errors as rejected promises.
Returns boolean (true when a row was affected, false when target missing or already deleted); propagates pool errors as rejected promises.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeavePolicyRepository must follow the same structural and behavioral conventions as the existing LeaveTypeRepository: same pool import path (../../shared/db/connection), same soft-delete filtering pattern (deleted_at IS NULL on all reads and updates), same dynamic addField/paramIndex update pattern, same softDelete returning (result.rowCount ?? 0) > 0, and same empty-update fallback to findById.

The leave-policy repository test must mirror the leave-type repository test's mocking approach: jest.mock on ../../../../src/shared/db/connection with pool.query as jest.fn, mockQuery.mockReset() in beforeEach, factory helpers for the entity and DTO, and assertions on exact SQL strings and parameter arrays.

The leave module barrel must continue to re-export the Phase 3 LeaveType symbols (LeaveType, CreateLeaveTypeDto, ILeaveTypeRepository, LeaveTypeRepository) unchanged while adding the four LeavePolicy symbols; existing exports must not be removed or renamed.

The repository must obtain its database connection by importing the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts — the same singleton pool used by LeaveTypeRepository and EmployeeRepository — and must not create a separate Pool instance.

The leave_policies persistence contract must match the conceptual table definition in ARCHITECTURE.md: columns policy_name, leave_type_id (FK→leave_types), entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at — with the soft-delete column (deleted_at) added to align with the established leave_types/employees pattern.

integrationPoints.why: The LeavePolicy model imports LeaveType to establish the cross-entity dependency declared in the Phase 4 task; LeavePolicy.leaveTypeId references a LeaveType row.
The repository executes all SQL through the shared PostgreSQL connection pool; this is the single integration point with the database adapter and satisfies GP-001.

All four LeavePolicy symbols must be re-exported through the module's public entry point so downstream phases (LeaveBalance in Phase 5, LeaveService in Phase 8) import them only via the barrel per the dependency rules.
The leave-policy repository test must follow the established mocking and assertion conventions from the leave-type test to keep the test suite consistent and maintainable.
